basis: Independent source, package, PE/resource and selected IL/disassembly review, with atomscan used to measure coverage and VT existing-hash reports used only as a second opinion. No sample application/native code executed, no C2 contacted, no samples uploaded to VT.
label_actions: Applied all 40 Hopper moves: labels.json. Ten benign originals relocated and hash-verified: moved-good.json.

notes: Bounded Node v26 SEA PE-resource extraction exposes JavaScript and embedded assets. Snapshot/unknown layouts fail closed; paths sanitized; resource/asset/count bounds checked.
Decoded compressed-data format is neutral; decoded child behavior still analyzed.
ELF non-UTF8 parser limitation is separated from malformed ELF headers.
Embedded PE physical span uses raw/certificate extents, not virtual SizeOfImage, preventing adjacent-member contamination.
Cache schema is 26. Local atomscan/cleave binaries rebuilt against sibling source; generated Cargo.lock overrides restored. Preserve pre-existing sibling changes.

trait_changes: Three Node native PE loader/header-erasure/encrypted-stager/indirect-syscall hostile composites, grounded in parser, FFI ABI, bound memory overwrite and stub array observations.
Python command-field alias selectors and real JSON keyword POST calls repair polling mesh-agent coverage.
Cua import environment-event warning captures conditional import telemetry; label is user beacon policy rather than invented stealer behavior.
Four generic registry observations relocated to neutral capabilities; stronger attack-context consumers kept.
Two exact Process Explorer vulnerable-driver YARA identities overridden to neutral inventory; abuse context still required.
Quicktype compressed data and Hpsvm ELF parser limitations no longer create suspicious findings.

notes: Full make validate passes, including hostile 780, benign 1863, does-nothing 176, performance 11, and remaining scenario suites.
Earlier validation run hit two unrelated timing outliers; both subsequent full runs passed.
Hostile trait count is not inflated to satisfy a quota: small fragments, policy-only beacons and partially recovered native loaders can have fewer than three hostile findings.
Purgatory means concrete missing payload/provenance evidence; no claim of proven hostile intent. Sparse warning counts are retained rather than manufactured.
Atomscan exit 1 means hostile detections, not scan failure; all 40 outer specimens returned records.

samples.reason: Importing computer calls record_event(module_init) when telemetry is enabled. Its declared dependency range permits cua-core 0.3.2, whose implementation enables telemetry by default on ordinary non-CI machines without an opt-out, persists an installation ID, captures the event and immediately flushes it to PostHog. Hostile label follows the user policy for default import beacons.
samples.limits: Static source verification, not observed network transmission. Version 0.3.2 respects DO_NOT_TRACK, environment/machine opt-outs and CI defaults; it disables GeoIP and person profiles and does not identify users. Minimum version 0.3.0 contains an erroneous from core import, which can prevent telemetry loading: its intended identify/capture implementation is not proof that it works in a clean environment. No claim all allowed dependency versions behave identically. This is a policy beacon label, not a credential-stealer claim.
